prompt:
A flat scan of a page from a student's laboratory report, plain white paper, printed black rules and printed characters, filling the frame. The page shows one Karnaugh map for the five-variable function F(A, B, C, D, E), laid out as a single array eight cells wide and four cells tall, all cells equal squares inside a printed border.

The eight column headers sit outside the top edge, one above each column, and read 000, 001, 011, 010, 110, 111, 101, 100 from left to right. A column header carries the values of A, C and E in that order: first character A, second C, third E.

The four row headers sit outside the left edge, one beside each row, and read 00, 01, 11, 10 from top to bottom. A row header carries the values of B and D in that order: first character B, second D.

A cell's minterm number is the five-bit binary number A B C D E, A most significant, assembled from that cell's own column header and row header.

Put one character in each of the thirty-two cells: a 1 in exactly the cells whose minterm number is 17, 3, 31, 5, 24, 0 or 14, and a 0 in all the rest.

The page carries nothing further -- no title, no algebraic expression, no encircled groups, no shading, no notes in the margins.

Ignoring artistic quality and styling, does the image actually show that? Answer NO only if it shows something else entirely -- a blank sheet, a page of prose, a photograph, or an unrelated image. Answer yes or no only.
